subject: Controlled fleet shelving request and canary acceptance criteria for AcmeHealth patch
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-01T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Controlled fleet shelving request and canary acceptance criteria for AcmeHealth patch

Team —

Goal: schedule a controlled micropatch (v2.3.1 -> v2.3.2) for the on-prem Redwood Private fleet serving Acme Health. This is a safety-oriented patch (KV cache eviction fix + small runtime NV kernel tweak). I want to run a narrow, observable canary and have a clear "shelving" (pause) authority and rollback triggers.

Proposed high-level plan:
- Canary scope: 5% of Acme-serving nodes (target 12 hosts across two AZs) for 45 minutes.
- Ramp: 5% -> 20% (if metrics stable) over 60 minutes, then full rollout in waves.
- Acceptance criteria (at canary phase):
  - Error rate delta <= +0.3% over baseline (30m window)
  - 95th P95 latency regression < +80ms; P99 must not exceed baseline by >150ms
  - No KV cache corruption events; read-hit ratio within 2% of baseline
  - GPU memory usage steady; no OOMs or CUDA driver warnings
- Rollback / shelving triggers: any of the above thresholds exceeded OR unexpected process crash >1 host in canary OR any critical customer alarm.
- Communication: Ops bridge (redwood-ops), Acme paging channel, and a dedicated #acme-patch Slack.
- Maintenance window: propose 2026-09-03 01:00–04:00 UTC to avoid Acme billing cutover at 03:00 UTC.

Attachments: shelving-plan-v1.xlsx (proposed host list + sequence), telemetry-baselines.pdf (current baselines).

Asks:
1) Neha — can you review the acceptance thresholds and approve the canary gating policy or propose edits?
2) Laura — confirm staffing for the 01:00 UTC window and who will own rollback authorization if Neha is on-call.
3) Vivek — any runtime kernel concerns with the NV tweak we should gate on?

I want to get an external-facing schedule to Acme by EOD tomorrow so they can confirm constraints.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-01T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Controlled fleet shelving request and canary acceptance criteria for AcmeHealth patch

Thanks Marcus — quick notes inline.

- Recommendation: start with a slightly larger initial canary (10%) but keep timeboxed checks: 10% for 30 minutes, then 30m manual check, then auto-ramp to 25% for 30 minutes before further ramp. This reduces variance noise.
- Add a KV cache validation step post-deploy: run a sample suite (script attached in runbook) to validate key namespaces and checksum consistency. If checksum mismatch >0.1% we shelve immediately.
- Require a manual sign-off after the first 30 minutes of canary from either me or the on-call senior engineer; automated ramp only after sign-off.
- Add a circuit breaker on batch inference tasks—if queue latency >500ms for two consecutive 5-minute windows, pause rollout.
- We should also include a short preflight that validates the quantization table used by the NV kernel tweak — Vivek pls confirm.

I can own the canary watch if Marcus is OK. I'll update JIRA OPS-1127 and add the runbook link.

Neha
Neha Kapoor
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir@acmehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, acme-ops@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-09-02T09:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Controlled fleet shelving request and canary acceptance criteria for AcmeHealth patch

Marcus — thanks for the heads-up and level-set. A few constraints from Acme side:

- Please avoid any activity between 02:30–03:30 UTC due to our nightly billing job; even short latency spikes there will trigger downstream reconciliation jobs.
- We prefer the canary to be limited to non-production read-only traffic (if possible) for the first 60 minutes. If a full production canary is required, please surface that explicitly so we can notify product owners.
- Emergency contact: +1-617-555-0134 (pager) and samir@acmehealth.com.
- Validation we need from Redwood during canary: end-to-end request success rate, tokenization errors, and a snapshot of inference request traces for two representative customers.

Attached: acme-ops-constraints.txt with blackout windows and a short checklist.

If you can push the start to 01:45 UTC and honor our 02:30–03:30 blackout window, we can make time for the manual sign-off you requested.

Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Health
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, acme-ops@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-09-03T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Controlled fleet shelving request and canary acceptance criteria for AcmeHealth patch

Samir — appreciate the constraints and the pager number, thank you. Finalized plan below (reflects Neha's runbook edits and your blackout window):

Final canary schedule (UTC):
- Preflight dry run: 2026-09-03 01:30–01:40 UTC (validation only, no traffic changes)
- Canary start: 2026-09-03 01:45 UTC — initial 10% canary (non-prod read-only routing where possible) for 30 minutes
- Manual sign-off window: 2026-09-03 02:15–02:30 UTC (Neha or designated senior on-call)
- Hold window: 2026-09-03 02:30–03:30 UTC (we will not push new waves during this blackout; we will observe metrics only)
- If canary passes manual sign-off we will resume at 03:30 UTC with a phased ramp (25% -> 50% -> full over 90 minutes).

Canary acceptance criteria (final):
- E2E success rate delta <= +0.3% over baseline (30m windows)
- Tokenization & parse errors = 0 (any occurrence triggers shelving)
- Latency: P95 regression < +80ms; P99 regression < +150ms
- KV checksum mismatch < 0.1%
- No OOMs, no GPU driver warnings
- Queue latency guard: <500ms for batch tasks (two consecutive 5-minute windows) or pause rollout

Owners and contacts:
- Canary watch: Neha Kapoor (primary) — neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
- Rollback authority: Laura Bennett (ops lead) — laura_bennett@redwood.ai
- Runtime kernel SME: Vivek Kulkarni — vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
- Acme emergency contact: Samir Patel (+1-617-555-0134)

Artifacts and links: shelving-plan-v1.xlsx, telemetry-baselines.pdf, acme-ops-constraints.txt, runbook https://drive.redwood.com/open?id=1a2b3c-shelving-plan, JIRA OPS-1127.

Neha — please confirm you approve the manual sign-off gate. Laura — confirm you'll accept rollback authority during the window. Once internal approvals are in place I'll send a brief schedule + playbook to Samir and the Acme ops list.

Thanks —
Marcus
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
